
## 1. Simulate data

<br>**Set seed to ensure replicability.**
<br>

```{r}
set.seed(12345)
```

<br>**This example uses simulated data, so it runs without any real data.**
<br>**Replace the simulation chunk and change the variable names.**
<br>

```{r}
n <- 600
true_class <- sample(1:3, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.5, .3, .2))

centres <- rbind(c(-1, -1, -1),   # profile 1: low on everything
                 c( 1,  1,  1),   # profile 2: high on everything
                 c( 1, -1,  0))   # profile 3: mixed

dat <- data.frame(
  x1 = rnorm(n, centres[true_class, 1], .6),
  x2 = rnorm(n, centres[true_class, 2], .6),
  x3 = rnorm(n, centres[true_class, 3], .6)
)
dat$outcome_a <- rnorm(n, c(0, .8, -.5)[true_class])
dat$outcome_b <- rnorm(n, c(.3, -.3, .6)[true_class])
```

<br>**Assign your dataset to dat so that the codes will run.**
<br>
```{r}
#dat <- df1

# Standardise the indicators
indicators <- c("x1", "x2", "x3")
dat[indicators] <- scale(dat[indicators])
```


## 2. Fit the LPA models

<br>**Please note that this chunk of code can take hours to run, depending on the number of participants in your dataset.**
<br>**Using 'cache_file` saves the fitted models so that you don't have to refit them during knitting.**
<br>**The lpa function has been set to run EEI and VVI models only.**
<br>

```{r}
profiles <- run_lpa(
  data       = dat,
  indicators = indicators,
  classes    = 1:4,
  variances  = c("equal", "varying"),
  cache_file = "lpa_models_example.rds"
)

fit_table(profiles)
```

<br>**Based on the results, you will have to choose the model that makes the most sense.**

## 3. Inspect the chosen solution

```{r}
chosen_profile <- profiles[["equal var 3"]]

class_sizes(chosen_profile)
avg_posterior(chosen_profile)
extract_profile_means(chosen_profile)
```

<br>**Look at the means, then name your profiles, instead of using "Profile A", "Profile B" etc.**
<br>**The names must match the class order shown above (`class1`, `class2`, ...).**
<br>**Replace "Indicator 1", "Indicator 2" etc. with your actual variable names.**
<br>**If your chosen solution has more than 3 classes, add "class4 = ..." in profile_labels.**

```{r}
profile_labels <- c(
  class1 = "Profile A",
  class2 = "Profile B",
  class3 = "Profile C"
)

plot_lpa_profiles(chosen_profile,
                  type           = "line",
                  profile_labels = profile_labels,
                  var_labels     = c(x1 = "Indicator 1", x2 = "Indicator 2", x3 = "Indicator 3"),
                  y_label        = "Standardised mean")
```

## 4. BCH: distal outcomes

<br>**This is the code to run all steps for one outcome at once.**
<br>**Replace outcome_a with the name of your auxiliary variable.**
<br>

```{r}
res_a <- bch_full(chosen_profile, dat$outcome_a, "Outcome A",
                  N = nrow(dat), profile_labels = profile_labels)
```

<br>**This is the code to run the BCH analysis step by step.**
<br>**Again, replace outcome_b with the name of your auxiliary variable.**
<br>**I have include codes to compute pairwise comparisons and effect sizes.**

```{r}
bch_b <- run_bch(chosen_profile, dat$outcome_b, "Outcome B", profile_labels)
bch_omnibus(bch_b, N = nrow(dat), "Outcome B")
bch_pairwise(bch_b, profile_labels, "Outcome B")
bch_effect_sizes(bch_b, class_sizes(chosen_profile), profile_labels, "Outcome B")
```

<br>**Use the code below to plot relevant outcomes together.**

```{r}
plot_bch_outcomes(list(res_a$bch, bch_b), profile_labels = profile_labels)

# Black-and-white version for print (needs ggpattern)
# plot_bch_outcomes(list(res_a$bch, bch_b), profile_labels = profile_labels, style = "pattern")
```
